content.text: The word 乗（ぬ）い物（むん）itself is derived by the combination of 乗（ぬ）いん / 乗（ぬ）ゆん = to ride with 物（むん or むぬ）.

When you want to say to ride on a certain vehicle, you use [vehicle] + んかい + 乗（ぬ）いん / 乗（ぬ）ゆん. To generalize it and say to ride on it or a non-vehicle thing, it becomes [object] +  上 + んかい + 乗（ぬ）いん / 乗（ぬ）ゆん. You can also use 馬乗い（んまぬい）for horseback riding.

In an earlier lesson, 上 was introduced as (っ)うぃー ((っ)ゐー is sometimes used). However, do note that Okinawan does have some dialects. For example, in Yomitan village you would say the same thing as うゎーび (sometimes written as っわーび) for up. For exams, it is ideal to stick with the main (Naha-Shuri) dialect, so keep it with the first.
